analysis.session_summary: The tape was dominated by a dollar-negative FOMC press conference: USD own-currency impulse was 0.242% lower, and DXY closed 0.327% lower. The ECB held rates at 2.65%, but Lagarde's press conference produced a +0.106% EUR impulse, fueling a 50.0-pip EUR/USD rally into the close. GBP, CAD, and CHF led while AUD lagged, closing weakest after an early attempt was rejected. A strong US GDP beat (3.4% vs 3.2%) was inverted, with USD still weakening 0.055%, reinforcing the dollar-negative tone.

themes.theme: FOMC press conference set a dollar-negative tone
themes.evidence: USD own-ccy impulse -0.242%; EUR/USD first leg +19.0 pips, USD/JPY first leg -56.4 pips, USD/SEK first leg -559.7 pips.

themes.theme: ECB hold to press conference rebound
themes.evidence: Refi inline at 2.65% still saw EUR -0.052%; ECB press conference impulse +0.106%, EUR/USD final leg +50.0 pips, EUR/GBP +9.1 pips.
VIX fell 0.926%; Brent first leg -1.642% then final leg +1.099%; USD/MXN gained 0.934% on geopolitical headlines.

currency_drivers.USD: FOMC press conference and GDP beat both produced USD weakness; broad dollar sold off.
currency_drivers.EUR: ECB held at 2.65% in line; Lagarde press conference sparked recovery from early weakness.
currency_drivers.JPY: No Japanese catalyst; yen led early then gave back 93%, closing little changed.
currency_drivers.GBP: No UK catalyst; strongest performer as its range held and USD slid.
currency_drivers.AUD: No Australian catalyst; AUD led early then gave back 92%, ending weakest.
currency_drivers.CAD: No Canadian catalyst; CAD strength tracked oil and broad USD softness.
currency_drivers.CHF: No Swiss catalyst; CHF closed at its best as EUR/CHF fell.
currency_drivers.NZD: No NZ catalyst; NZD selling rejected 77%, still soft as USD weakness offset.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped through a 19.0-pip FOMC bounce, a -25.9 and -29.8 pip drift, then a 50.0-pip ECB press conference rally into the close.

polarity_reads.read: Beat (+3.4% vs 3.2%) produced USD weakness 0.055%, implying USD positive data surprises were faded; market positioned for USD downside/risk-on.
Inline hold at 2.65% still saw EUR weaken 0.052%; no policy impulse, with initial EUR selling before the press conference.
Unscored but USD weaker 0.242%; move driven by Warsh's tone, not a data surprise.
Unscored but EUR stronger 0.106%; Lagarde's comments were read as constructive, reversing the rate-decision dip.
No-data with no quotes around the release; cannot infer a polarity from the 4.00% inline print.

scenarios.thesis: Post-FOMC dollar softness continues as BOJ is unlikely to rescue USD; high-beta pairs extend.
triggers: BOJ keeps policy unchanged and statement less hawkish
Tokyo core CPI prints at or below 2.6%
scenarios.invalidation: BOJ surprises hawkish or US Employment Cost Index tops 0.8%.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD closed near highs of 68.8-pip range; trend continuation within that range.

scenarios.name: Risk rebound extends
scenarios.thesis: Risk appetite improves; commodity FX recovers while USD remains soft; AUD/NZD selling is rejected.
scenarios.invalidation: Iran/Hormuz headlines escalate or VIX spikes above today's high.

NZD selling rejected 77%; 31.3-pip range likely retests upper half.
